subject.title: fix(anthropic): restrict OAuth callback host to loopback addresses and derive redirect URI

question: Should Anthropic OAuth now fail closed to localhost, 127.0.0.1, or ::1 callback hosts and derive redirect_uri from that host, despite rejecting non-loopback OPENCLAW_OAUTH_CALLBACK_HOST values that current releases accept?
rationale: The code fix is narrow and source-backed, but it changes a shipped env/default auth-provider behavior and the original security framing depends on OpenClaw's trusted-operator environment model.

options.title: Accept Loopback-Only Anthropic OAuth
options.body: Approve the fail-closed callback-host validation because arbitrary remote callback hosts are not a supported local CLI auth shape and the PR follows the sibling OAuth pattern.

options.title: Require Live Provider Exchange Proof
options.body: Ask for redacted live Anthropic exchange proof before accepting provider-side redirect registration risk for each allowed loopback spelling.

options.title: Pause Direct Anthropic OAuth Direction
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers prefer removing or deprecating the direct Anthropic OAuth helper instead of hardening it now.

recommendation.title: Accept Loopback-Only Anthropic OAuth
recommendation.body: Approve the fail-closed callback-host validation because arbitrary remote callback hosts are not a supported local CLI auth shape and the PR follows the sibling OAuth pattern.
